headline: gas-led spot at a fresh three-year high, up 85% in a year, as renewed US-Iran tension lifts European gas; next winter is the expensive part of the curve
commentary: UK power spot has hit 137.72 GBP/MWh, a fresh three-year high and up 85% on a year ago. The driver this week is geopolitical: renewed US-Iran hostilities have pushed European TTF gas above 75 euros/MWh, its highest since early 2023, and that feeds straight into the UK gas and power curves. The NBP forward strip has moved up across the board, with Winter 26 around 181 p/therm. What matters for tender timing is the curve's shape: next winter is the expensive part, with Summer 27 (119.75) and Winter 27 (116.60) priced roughly a third below Winter 26. A 12-month term starting this October sits on that winter; a 24-month blends it with a cheaper 2027/28, so the longer terms are pricing better per kWh. With the near-term move driven by a geopolitical risk that can't be timed, the question is term length, not waiting for a lower entry.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Oct 26) is 180.78 p/therm and the winter strip is higher still (Winter 26 at 181.25). This week's leg up tracks European TTF gas breaking above 75 euros/MWh on the renewed US-Iran conflict. Summer 27 (119.75) and Winter 27 (116.60) sit roughly a third lower, so next winter is the expensive part of the curve.
